channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: US Kok-Boru Team Honors First Coach in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The U.S. Kok-Boru team, led by captain Ladd Howell, visited the home of their first coach, Mirlan Srazhdinov, to honor his memory. The team presented commemorative gifts to the family and fondly recalled their mentor, who facilitated connections between American and Kyrgyz players. Srazhdinov was a player and captain for the 'Börülü' team and represented Kyrgyzstan at the first World Nomad Games.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Non-Tax Budget Revenues Show Significant Growth
item.description: Non-tax revenues in Kyrgyzstan's budget have increased significantly, reaching 189.5 billion soms in 2025, an 88 billion som rise from the previous year. This growth raised the share of non-tax revenues in GDP from 6.4% to 9.6%. Key sources include dividends from state shares, National Bank profits, state service fees, and other non-tax collections. Projections estimate non-tax revenues at 149.2 billion soms in 2027 and 189.9 billion by 2031.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Ban on Under-16s Using Social Media
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering a ban on social media registration for individuals under 16, with a draft law submitted to parliament. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized the need to protect children from the influence of social media, digital platforms, and AI, citing similar measures in other countries. He also called for enhanced content filtering and the expansion of dedicated children's SIM cards to ensure 'information immunity'.

item.title: Bishkek section of Chui Avenue to close for World Nomad Games and SCO summit
item.description: A section of Chui Avenue in Bishkek will be closed to traffic from August 27 to August 29. The closure is due to security measures for the upcoming 6th World Nomad Games and the SCO summit. Drivers are advised to plan alternative routes. The SCO summit is scheduled for August 31 and September 1, with the World Nomad Games running from August 31 to September 6.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to acquire 9 hectares of land in China's Xi'an for transport center
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to build a transport and logistics center in Xi'an, China, acquiring a 9-hectare plot of land. The center will be part of the Xi'an—Kashgar—Osh multimodal route, facilitating cargo transport by rail and road. This initiative aims to launch new routes and increase freight volumes before the China—Kyrgyzstan—Uzbekistan railway becomes operational.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's State Budget Revenue Expected to Reach 1.15 Trillion Som by 2031
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's state budget revenues are projected to reach 791.1 billion som in 2027 and are planned to increase to 1 trillion 148.6 billion som by 2031, according to the Ministry of Finance's fiscal and investment policy report. The ministry forecasts that budget revenues will decrease as a percentage of GDP from 28.9% in 2027 to 23.1% in 2031. State budget expenditures are expected to rise from 758.7 billion som in 2027 to 1 trillion 49.4 billion som in 2031.

item.title: Kyrgyzpharmatsiya Plans Direct Procurement of Spinal Implants from Turkish Company
item.description: State Enterprise 'Kyrgyzpharmatsiya' and Turkish company Mikron Medical have signed a memorandum of understanding to cooperate in supplying orthopedic and spinal implants to Kyrgyzstan's medical institutions. Kyrgyzpharmatsiya believes direct cooperation with manufacturers will reduce intermediaries and potentially lower procurement costs. The Turkish company's products are being considered for centralized medical device procurement in 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's state budget revenue projected to reach 1.15 trillion soms by 2031
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Finance forecasts state budget revenues to reach 791.1 billion soms in 2027 and increase to 1.1486 trillion soms by 2031. The budget's share of GDP is expected to decrease from 28.9% in 2027 to 23.1% in 2031. Expenditures are projected to rise from 758.7 billion soms in 2027 to 1.0494 trillion soms in 2031.

item.title: CIA Director reportedly visited Moscow to warn against attacking NATO
item.description: The Director of the CIA reportedly made an unannounced visit to Moscow to warn Russia against attacking NATO member states, particularly Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. This warning comes amid concerns that Russia might test the alliance's strength. Neither Washington nor Moscow officially announced the visit or its agenda.

item.title: New Kazakhstan Entry Rules: Kyrgyz Citizens Can Still Travel Freely
item.description: Kazakhstan is implementing new digital migration mechanisms, including a preliminary entry approval system (QazETA) and a unified information database. While the Ministry of Internal Affairs plans a phased rollout from August to December 2026, potentially with service fees, Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs clarified that Kyrgyz citizens currently do not require preliminary approval for travel to Kazakhstan. Discussions are underway to analyze EAEU agreements.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Changes Family Assistance Benefit Rules Effective September 1
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will modify the criteria for granting the 'family assistance' benefit to low-income families with children under 16, effective September 1. The minimum guaranteed income will increase from 1,000 to 1,500 som. Families with cars older than 15 years will be eligible, while those owning two or more residences will be excluded. Norms for calculating income from land shares will also be updated.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers VAT Exemption for QR Payments and Phone Transfers
item.description: Kazakhstan's financial regulators are proposing to extend the existing VAT exemption for payment card operations to cover QR code payments and phone number transfers. This move aims to create equal conditions for various cashless payment methods as digital options gain popularity. The Ministry of National Economy is involved in the discussion, with further analysis by the Ministry of Finance, the Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market, and the National Bank.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discussed as Responsible Middle Power at ISMI Seminar
item.description: The Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies (ISMI) hosted a seminar on "Uzbekistan as a Responsible Middle Power," marking the country's 35th independence anniversary. The event focused on a new analytical report detailing Uzbekistan's foreign policy evolution and changes over the years, particularly in the last decade. Participants included government officials and academics.

item.title: Memorandum Signed to Study Renewable Energy Projects in Uzbekistan
item.description: Saudi company ACWA Power and South Korean Korea Western Power Co., Ltd. (KOWEPO) signed a memorandum in Tashkent to explore renewable energy opportunities in Uzbekistan. The agreement aims to jointly assess prospects for renewable energy projects, energy storage systems, and related infrastructure, potentially attracting South Korean investment.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan Share Common Regional Strategic Interests, Official States
item.description: Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan are united by common regional strategic interests, according to Azerbaijani Member of Parliament Shakhin Seidzade. He stated that the recent state visit of Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev to Tashkent signifies a new stage in bilateral relations, moving beyond traditional cooperation to become a key component of broader regional processes.

item.title: Teenager with Schizophrenia on Trial in Aktobe for Mother's Murder
item.description: A 16-year-old teenager diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia is on trial in Aktobe for allegedly murdering his mother and injuring his grandmother. Specialists concluded he was not aware of his actions at the time of the crime. The prosecution alleges a prolonged family conflict preceded the incident, leading to the fatal stabbing.

item.title: New Gas Block Production Plant Launched in Uzbekistan's Fergana Region
item.description: A new gas block production plant has been launched in the Dangara district of Uzbekistan's Fergana region. The project, implemented with $40 million in foreign investment, is equipped with advanced technologies and has created 80 new jobs. This initiative expands production capacity in the construction materials sector.

item.title: Russia Plans Escalation of Ukraine Conflict, Targeting Kyiv and Infrastructure
item.description: Russian authorities reportedly plan to escalate the war against Ukraine, potentially using ballistic missiles against central Kyiv and energy infrastructure elsewhere, according to Bloomberg citing sources close to the Kremlin. This decision stems from President Vladimir Putin's assessment of a deadlock in negotiations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Pistachio Plantations with Iranian Expertise
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish large pistachio plantations by developing desert and steppe zones, inviting 50 specialists from Iran. These experts are assessing land in Bukhara and other regions for planting high-yield, low-growing pistachio varieties suitable for steppe conditions. Drip irrigation technology will be used.

item.title: Uzbekistan focuses on crime prevention in local communities
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing new mechanisms for analyzing crime situations and predicting criminal activity within its internal affairs bodies. The head of state has prioritized timely prevention of offenses in every mahalla. This approach shifts the focus from solely law enforcement to a broader responsibility involving employment, education, healthcare, and local authorities in addressing crime-generating factors.

item.title: Foreign national arrested in Osh for attempting to bribe police officer
item.description: A foreign national has been detained in Osh, Kyrgyzstan, for attempting to bribe a police officer. The individual, who was working in the city without proper registration and permits, was issued a protocol. Instead of obtaining the necessary documents, the man offered a bribe to the officer to continue residing illegally. A criminal case for bribery has been initiated.

item.title: 232 Kazakh citizens awarded "Bolashak" scholarships for international study
item.description: A total of 232 Kazakh citizens have been awarded "Bolashak" scholarships for international study. Of these, 179 will pursue master's degrees, 12 doctoral degrees, one a bachelor's degree, and 40 will undertake professional internships abroad. Additionally, 33 individuals received "Scientific Internships" grants. Lists of recipients will be published on August 27.

item.title: Tashkent University of Applied Sciences expands international cooperation in higher education
item.description: Tashkent University of Applied Sciences (TAFU), celebrating its fifth anniversary, is among the top five private institutions in Uzbekistan whose graduates receive state-standard diplomas. The university currently enrolls over 20,000 students taught by more than 500 professors. TAFU aims to prepare specialists competitive both domestically and internationally, emphasizing the importance of qualified faculty.

item.title: Bishkek to Close Chuy Avenue for Two Days for Major Events
item.description: A section of Chuy Avenue in Bishkek will be closed to traffic from August 27 to August 29. The closure is to ensure security during preparations for the World Nomad Games and the SCO summit. Authorities have asked drivers to plan alternative routes.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Singapore Sign Agreements on Water, Transport, and Trade Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan and Singapore have agreed to cooperate in water management, transport, and trade. Agreements were signed during a meeting between President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong. The countries aim to enhance their dynamic relationship, which saw bilateral trade near $1 billion last year.

item.title: Urgench-Khiva Toll Road Cost Increases from $120 Million to $150 Million
item.description: The construction cost of Uzbekistan's first toll road, connecting Urgench and Khiva, has risen from $120 million to $150 million. The increased cost was announced during a ceremony attended by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The road is expected to boost tourism in the Khorezm region.

item.title: Chinese Expert Praises Uzbekistan's Development and Reforms Under 'New Uzbekistan' Model
item.description: Ma Bin, director of Fudan University's Center for Russian and Central Asian Studies, congratulated Uzbekistan on its upcoming 35th Independence Day. He highlighted Uzbekistan's "New Uzbekistan" model, emphasizing reforms in politics, economics, and foreign policy since 2016, which have led to significant transformations.

item.title: Uzbek President Awards State Decorations for Independence Anniversary
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented state awards to citizens on August 26, marking the 35th anniversary of Uzbekistan's independence. He highlighted the nation's progress over the past decade, noting over $160 billion in foreign investment, a 2.5-fold increase in economy size, and the creation of 5.7 million jobs. Significant infrastructure development includes new schools, hospitals, and improved water supply for millions.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Initiatives in SCO Focus on Economy and Security
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively contributing to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), focusing on security, trade-economic cooperation, industrial and technological collaboration, cultural-humanitarian ties, and regional connectivity. The SCO, celebrating its 25th anniversary, has expanded significantly and continues to attract growing interest from other nations seeking membership or partnership.

item.title: Mongolian President Visits Uzbekistan's National Pavilion in Ulaanbaatar
item.description: Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh visited Uzbekistan's National Pavilion at the 17th session of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (COP17) in Ulaanbaatar. He was briefed on Uzbekistan's environmental reforms and exchanged views on environmental protection and climate change cooperation. The Mongolian side expressed readiness to strengthen bilateral cooperation on these issues.

item.title: Mausoleum of Ydyrys-Ata in Jalal-Abad Region to Be Renovated
item.description: A design project is being developed to renovate the historical and cultural pilgrimage site of Ydyrys-Ata in the Chaktal district of Jalal-Abad region. The Ministry of Construction, Architecture, and Housing and Communal Services aims to preserve cultural heritage, improve the territory, and create conditions for pilgrims and tourists, thereby boosting local tourism.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Health proposes transferring drug storage to Kyrgyzpharma
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Health proposes transferring the storage and distribution of humanitarian aid and state-procured medicines from the Department of Medicines and Medical Devices to the state enterprise "Kyrgyzpharma." This move aims to separate regulatory and economic functions within the ministry's subordinate organizations. The draft changes are currently open for public discussion. Kyrgyzpharma was established in 2023 to ensure transparent procurement and supply of medicines for state hospitals.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy proposes revising deposit protection rules
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy and Commerce has proposed amendments to the Law "On Protection of Bank Deposits." The current deposit protection system, in place since 2008, has not seen rule changes in 17 years. With a sevenfold increase in deposits since 2020, the insurance fund's coverage ratio has dropped to 4.3%, below the legal minimum of 12%. The ministry suggests introducing new, risk-based tariffs for banks and microfinance organizations.

item.title: Navoiy region imports labor from other Uzbek regions, says governor
item.description: Navoiy region governor Normat Tursunov announced that over 50,000 people from other regions of Uzbekistan are working in Navoiy. He stated this during a ceremony for the launch of new facilities attended by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The governor linked this labor import to the region's economic development and the creation of new production capacities. He also reported on the launch of a 300 MW solar generation project and a 150 MW energy storage project in Nurata district.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Acquires 9 Hectares in Xi'an for Transport and Logistics Center
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is acquiring a 9-hectare land plot in Xi'an, China, to establish a transport and logistics center. This center will be part of the Xi'an-Kashgar-Osh multimodal route, facilitating cargo transport via rail and road. The project aims to increase freight volumes and revenue for Kyrgyzstan's railway sector even before the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is completed.

item.title: Uzbekneftgaz to Strengthen Control Over Joint Ventures Amid Production Declines
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz has begun systematically inspecting and intensifying control over its joint ventures due to declining production volumes and issues with dividend payments. The company cited insufficient regulation, lack of transparency in accounting, and unfulfilled dividend obligations as problems. This intensified oversight aims to address these issues.

item.title: Uzbek President: Lack of Political Will Led to Cotton 'Slavery'
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated that a lack of political will previously forced the country into a system where cotton cultivation dominated all aspects of life, including child labor in fields. He noted that reforms have since freed Uzbekistan from this 'cotton slavery'.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Modifies 'Uyi-Bulogo Komok' Benefit Criteria Effective September 1
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has amended the criteria for the 'Uyi-Bulogo Komok' monthly benefit for families with children under 16, effective September 1, 2026. Changes include increasing the guaranteed minimum income threshold and introducing new criteria related to vehicle age and property ownership.

item.title: Russia Implements New Medical Examination Rules for Migrants Effective September 2026
item.description: Starting September 1, 2026, Russia will integrate migrant medical examination results into a unified health ministry system, accessible to the Interior Ministry. Migrants must undergo examinations within 30 days of entry. Failure to comply or detection of dangerous diseases may lead to expulsion.

item.title: US Temporarily Halts Immigration Visa Applications for Potential Public Charge Candidates
item.description: The US administration has temporarily suspended the processing of immigration visa applications worldwide to train consular officers in identifying candidates likely to become a public charge. Applicants with scheduled interviews have been notified of postponements, with new dates to be announced later. This measure is part of stricter entry policies.
